idea-plugin.name: SQL String Concatenation Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags SQL queries built by unparameterized string concatenation or interpolation -- the classic SQL-injection shape -- in Java, Kotlin, and Python, and offers a real quick-fix toward parameterization.

What triggers it (both conditions required):

  • A string literal that looks like the start of a real SQL statement (SELECT/INSERT/ UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/ WITH, or CREATE/ALTER/ DROP/TRUNCATE), built with +, a Kotlin template, a Python f-string, .format() or % from a value that could carry injected SQL -- e.g. "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'" (Java/Kotlin), "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $userId" (Kotlin template), f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}" (Python), or "... WHERE id = %s" % user_id.
  • The resulting string is used near a call that looks like it executes SQL: Statement.executeQuery/executeUpdate/execute, cursor.execute/executemany (Python DB-API), rawQuery (Android), createQuery/createNativeQuery, and .query(...).

What does NOT trigger it (the anti-false-positive design, see README for the full worked list):

  • Literals and constants ("SELECT * FROM " + TABLE_USERS + " WHERE id = ?"), numbers (an int parameter, %d placeholders), and locals last assigned a literal.
  • A SQL-keyword-shaped string with no nearby execution call -- a log message -- and commented-out code.
  • A value already parameterized correctly (? placeholders with PreparedStatement.setX(...), or a DB-API parameter tuple like cursor.execute(query, (param,))).

On 271 public Java, Kotlin and Python files that execute SQL, 28 of a random sample of 30 warnings were real queries built from a variable.

Where it fits: IntelliJ IDEA with Database Tools has a built-in data-flow inspection for Java/Kotlin ("Non-safe string is used as SQL"); with both on you'll see two warnings on the same line. Without it -- IntelliJ IDEA without Database Tools, Android Studio, PyCharm -- this plugin works on its own, with no server and no build.

Quick-fix, honest scope: replaces the interpolated value with a ? placeholder and adds a TODO(sql-concat) comment naming the variable that still needs to be bound as a real parameter (.setString(1, ...)/cursor.execute(query, (param,))). It does not infer the value's real type or its correct positional index across a multi-placeholder query -- stated here rather than pretended to be handled.

Deliberately narrow (not a full SAST scanner like Qodana): one specific pattern, near-zero configuration, tuned hard against false positives.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
